title: Variables and unified conditions
description: Numeric/string game variables alongside boolean flags: set_var/add_var commands, vars in SimState (serializable). Unified 'when' condition object usable on interactions, choice options, triggers, and commands: {flag, notFlag, var comparisons (eq/ne/lt/gte...), all/any/not composition}. requiresFlag/forbidsFlag stay as sugar (backward compatible; existing games untouched). Validation cross-checks referenced vars/flags with actionable errors.
close_reason: Implemented vars + unified when conditions. SimState.vars (number|string record, snapshot-safe, tolerant fromSnapshot). Commands set_var/add_var (missing var starts at 0; add-on-text is a static validation error when every set_var writes text, runtime event otherwise; writing built-in 'money' var errors). When = {flag}|{notFlag}|{var,op eq/ne/lt/lte/gt/gte,value}|{all}|{any}|{not} via zod lazy union (strict variants), evaluated by exported evalWhen(ctx={flags,vars,money}); missing vars read 0/'' by value type, type mismatches only satisfy ne, 'money' built-in readable. Optional when on EVERY command (shared command() helper, silently skipped) and on interactions (ANDed with requiresFlag/forbidsFlag sugar). Validation warns on vars read-never-written and flags read-never-set (trainer defeatFlags count as writes); demo+emberwood pinned at zero errors/warnings. 43 new tests (vars.test.ts + gating coverage); npm test 237 green, tsc clean in engine+play.

title: Acceptance: build a new game entirely through the Forge
description: Fresh-eyes test: author a small complete game (2-3 maps, catalog subset, one boss, winnable) using ONLY forge tools + playtest gates — no hand-written JSON. Report friction; file beads for every rough edge found.
close_reason: Built 'Saltmere Light' (games/saltmere-light) 100% through forge MCP tools from the blank template — zero hand-written JSON. 3 maps (harbor/cliff-path/lighthouse) via portals, 5-species 4-type catalog with glimmerling->lanternjaw evolution line, wild encounters on cliff-path, LOS trainer Piet + gate trainer Oda, boss Warden Maris behind a flag-barred door, spatial chandlery shop + 3 free heal points, win on the flag-gated lamp. Gates: forge_check pass; forge_playtest explore (default seed) win=true in 95 steps 8/8 battles (boss survived at 6/32 HP — earnest); golden-path script wins at turn 63; seeds 1/3/4/5 also win. npm run validate clean; web dev server glob discovers the game. ~100 tool calls over the session. Friction filed: llm-rpg-85g.10 (guide/linkPortal bidirectional contradiction), 85g.11 (rejected batch renders discarded draft state), 85g.12 (schema field docs missing; README species example lacks types), 85g.13 (no per-battle detail in playtest reports), 85g.14 (stopDetail hides gate-trainer blocker), 85g.15 (blank template missing ',' road tile), 85g.16 (multi-seed sweep for tuning), 85g.17 (LOS overlay in forge_map), llm-rpg-3pj (interact targeting ambiguity, cost a scripted win). Verdict: promise holds — a mid-tier LLM with only guide+tools could ship this; every rejection named its fix, and the explore harness caught both my type-chart design bug and the impossible-boss math.

title: Turn-based battle engine
description: Deterministic battle sim over a catalog: fight/switch/run actions, speed-based turn order (RNG ties), pokemon-style damage formula with STAB + type effectiveness + 0.85-1.0 roll, accuracy checks, PP, fainting, wild + trainer modes. Pure module, no I/O; seeded RNG.
close_reason: battle.ts: deterministic Battle class, all randomness via injected Rng. Damage floor((floor((2L/5+2)*power*atk/max(1,def))/50+2)*stab*typeMult*roll), STAB 1.5, roll U[0.85,1.0], min 1 dmg when typeMult>0. Turn order by stage-modified spd, rng tiebreak. Escape chance clamp(0.5+0.1*(pSpd-eSpd)/max(1,eSpd), 0.1, 0.95) using stage-free spd, wild only. PP decrements; 0-PP move rejected without consuming round; all-PP-exhausted falls back to built-in Flail (normal/20/never misses). Faint -> needsSwitch free switch (no enemy hit); voluntary switch gives enemy a free attack; enemy auto-replaces. Swappable EnemyAi (default random valid move). state fully JSON-serializable with outcome ongoing/player_won/enemy_won/fled. 15 battle tests pass incl determinism, effectiveness ratios, STAB, seeded miss/run, trainer-forbids-run.

title: Creature catalogs: species/moves/type-chart schemas + sample dataset

close_reason: catalog.ts: Zod schemas (TypeChart/Move/Species/Catalog) + validateCatalog with fix-naming errors (unknown types/moveIds/evolution targets, dup ids, unsorted learnset, missing level-1 move, bad multipliers). Decisions: type chart supports PARTIAL coverage — missing pairs default to 1.0 so only non-neutral matchups need listing; single atk/def pair so physical/special is descriptive; move effects kept minimal as one-stage raise_/lower_ atk/def/spd (raise targets self, lower targets opponent) so status moves do something. Helpers: speciesById, moveById, statsAtLevel (hp=floor(2b*L/100)+L+10, others +5), movesKnownAtLevel (last 4), typeMultiplier. Fixture test/fixtures/catalog.json: 6 types, 13 moves, 8 species incl emberling->pyrewyrm line, mosskrag dual rock/grass, puddlit. 11 catalog tests pass.

title: Engine: interact target ambiguous with multiple adjacent entities (not facing-based, undocumented)
description: Standing at lighthouse (4,2) between the-great-lamp (4,1, north) and warden-maris (4,3, south) in saltmere-light: after a north bump into the lamp ('The Great Lamp is standing there. Try interact'), 'interact' targeted Maris instead. Target selection with 2+ adjacent entities appears to be list-order (or fixed direction order), not last-faced, and no doc states the rule. This cost a scripted playtest its win; workaround was approaching the lamp from a tile where it is the only neighbor. Fix: prefer the entity in the last-moved/bumped direction, or document the deterministic order in README + forge.md so script authors can plan.

title: Playtest reports: no per-battle detail; lastEvents window too small to diagnose a lost fight
description: Explore/script reports summarize battles as {fought, won, lost, fled} with only the final ~20 events. In the 85g.6 tuning loop, 'lost: 1' gave no way to see WHICH battle was lost, to whom, at what levels/HP — diagnosing the boss fight required hand-crafting a script that ends exactly at the fight so lastEvents happens to cover it. Wanted: a battles[] list (opponent entity id or 'wild <species>', map, start/end step, result, player party levels/HP after) and/or an events budget parameter / full-log option on forge_playtest. Related: llm-rpg-aiw.19 (script divergence diagnostics).

title: Forge: rejected batch response renders the discarded draft state (validation OK + map render)
description: When forge_batch rejects (all-or-nothing, 'NOTHING was written'), the response still appends 'validation: OK — the game is fully valid and playable' plus an ASCII render of the touched map — both computed from the rolled-back draft, not the on-disk file. In the 85g.6 run the render showed a fully-built harbor map while games/<dir>/game.json still had zero maps (a following forge_map call errored 'unknown map'). An LLM reading that response can easily conclude the batch half-landed. Fix: after a rejection, report the persisted state (or omit render/validation and say 'state unchanged').

title: Forge guide: portal workflow contradicts linkPortal (bidirectional to missing map is rejected)
description: docs/forge.md step 3 says 'Link portals as you go (linkPortal, usually bidirectional: true). A portal to a not-yet-created map is a normal draft state' — but linkPortal with bidirectional:true REJECTS when the destination map does not exist ('bidirectional needs map X to exist'). Only one-way dangling links are draft-able. Either fix the guide (link one-way while drafting, add the return link after createMap) or make the op queue the reverse half until the map exists. Found in 85g.6 acceptance run: first map batch died on its final op because of this.

notes:
engine half done: new command { type:'passage', title?, lines[] (min 1), citation?, when? }. Execution appends {title?,lines,citation?} to state.lastPassages (new SimState array, cleared at the START of every act() exactly like lastEvents, snapshot-safe, fromSnapshot defaults it for old snapshots) AND pushes one formatted multi-line event string: title, blank line, lines, then '— citation' if present — so CLI/MCP/text observers work unchanged. observe.ts prints multi-line events in full (each inner line indented), never truncated. Tests: packages/engine/test/passage.test.ts (formatting, lastPassages lifecycle incl. guard-path clearing, when gating, snapshots, observer output). Web half remaining: styled keypress-paged text pane rendering state.lastPassages, distinct from the chatter box.
web half done: apps/web/src/ui/passage.ts (PassagePane) — full-stage dark serif reading pane, small-caps gold heading, verse hanging-indent lines, right-aligned muted em-dash citation, roman page indicator (ii / iv), bobbing advance marker. Pages measured against the pane for real (handles wrapping); citation joins the final page or takes its own. Enter/Space/E/z or click advances; all other game input blocked while open; MessageBox gains a gate so ordinary chatter holds until the reading closes, then plays. main.ts pumps sim.state.lastPassages each frame (feature-detected, splice-consumed; no-ops with zero errors on pre-passage engines). overworld.ts filters the engine's mirrored multi-line passage event out of the chatter box by exact re-render match (fails open). Dev hook: ?passagetest=1 (src/passagetest.ts, import.meta.hot-guarded like forge) queues Job 38 samples; verified tree-shaken — dist grep for hook + sample text = zero hits. CDP-verified: 12-line pagination (i/ii -> ii/ii), input blocking, queued second untitled passage w/ stanza break, clean close; end-to-end via throwaway games/passagetest NPC 'passage' command rendered a real passage (dir deleted after). vite build + tsc clean.
close_reason: Both halves complete: engine (passage command + lastPassages, tests) and web (PassagePane scripture-mode pane, measured pagination, input blocking, chatter gate, tree-shaken ?passagetest=1 dev hook). End-to-end verified via a real NPC passage interaction in a throwaway game.

Verified: tsc clean, vite build clean, headless CDP walkthrough (starter -> wild battle won -> trainer LOS battle won -> defeat/respawn -> win banner) with zero console errors.

title: Save/load sessions
description: Serialize full sim state (map, position, flags, party, inventory, RNG state) to JSON; load resumes identically. CLI/MCP save+load tools.
close_reason: Save/load shipped: Sim.fromSnapshot restores position/map/flags/party/inventory/money/battle (mid-battle, aliasing repaired after JSON) /rng/seed; engine save.ts codec { gameId, gameVersion, snapshot } — wrong gameId errors actionably, version mismatch warns but loads; play CLI save/load [slot] (default quick, <gameDir>/saves/, gitignored) + replay --from <slot>; MCP save_game/load_game tools; 6 tests in save.test.ts incl. mid-wild-battle and mid-trainer-battle round-trips and identical-continuation checks.

title: Items, inventory, shops, healing
description: Item catalog (heal, capture, key items), player inventory, use-in-battle and overworld, shop interaction commands, heal-center command.
notes: Battle-item core DONE (this session): Item schema in catalog (kind heal/capture, amount/ballMod/price, per-kind validation), player.inventory + money in GameSchema, give_item/give_money/heal_party commands, in-battle item use (item1..item9 consumes the turn; heal capped; capture rolls catch), catch consumes first capture item, inventory shown in battle observer. REMAINING for this bead: shop interactions (buy/sell commands using item.price and money), heal-center content convention beyond the heal_party command (e.g. named hearth entity pattern in Emberwood maps), overworld (out-of-battle) heal item use, key items / passive effects (keepers' charm +catch rate).
close_reason: Shops shipped (battle-item core was already done per earlier note): sell command { itemId, price } — player buys 1x for price with money check and shortfall-naming event; validateGame cross-checks itemId and enforces non-negative price; spatial counters (one interaction/entity per item, no menus); demo village gains Peddler Sela (embersalve 10c) and a snare stall (kindling-snare 20c); tests for buy success, insufficient money, per-counter items, and validation. Consciously left out -> follow-up llm-rpg-t9a: overworld (out-of-battle) heal item use, key items / keepers' charm passive catch bonus, player-sells-to-shop buyback. Heal-center convention: heal_party hearth entity pattern already in demo.

title: Trainer NPCs: parties, line-of-sight battles
description: Entity type trainer with party + defeat flag; line-of-sight engagement on overworld; trainer battle mode (no run, no catch); reward money/flags on victory.
close_reason: Trainer NPCs shipped: EntitySchema.trainer (party 1..6, defeatFlag, lineOfSight dir+range, rewardMoney, rewardCommands, intro/defeatText/outro); validateGame cross-checks party species + rewardCommands; interact- and LoS-triggered trainer battles (blocked by non-walkable tiles/blocking entities); no run/catch enforced, capture items not consumed; victory sets flag + pays rewards; defeated trainers act as NPCs (outro fallback); defeat uses respawn flow; multi-member enemy parties auto-send with XP per faint; demo Trailhand Ivo on east-road; 19 tests in trainer.test.ts; pinned winning script unchanged (Ivo watches row 3, script uses row 2).

title: Party, catching, XP, leveling, evolution
description: Player party (max 6), capture mechanics (catchRate + ball modifier + HP factor), XP yield -> level curve -> stat growth, learnset move acquisition, evolution on level. Party state serializable.
close_reason: Party (max 6) via player.party + give_species; catching p=clamp(catchRate*ballMod*(1.3-hp/maxHp),0.05,0.95), full-party catches gently released; XP floor(xpYield*enemyLevel/5) on enemy faint, cubic L^3 curve, level-ups recompute stats (heal by HP gain) and learn learnset moves replacing the OLDEST of 4; evolution checked at battle end keeping hp fraction. Demo migrated with embedded catalog + Elder gift; all state serializable.

title: Wire wild encounters into overworld sim
description: pendingEncounter from wild tiles launches a battle (wild mode); battle outcome flows back into sim state (flee/faint/victory). Whole-game action replay stays deterministic.
close_reason: Wild-tile hits now construct a wild Battle immediately (shared Rng, party by reference); battle actions gated both ways (move1..4/m, switch1..6/s, item1..9, catch/snare, run); outcomes flow back (victory->XP/evolution, defeat->heal+respawn+half money, fled); pendingEncounter/resolve removed; snapshot() includes battle state and is JSON-round-trippable; determinism through battles covered by tests (79 passing).

title: Passage pane polish: shared passage-event rendering + reading niceties
description: Follow-ups from the djt.7 web half. (1) The web drops the engine's mirrored multi-line passage event from the chatter box by re-rendering each lastPassages entry and exact-matching the string (apps/web/src/ui/overworld.ts withoutPassageEvents). If the engine's formatting in sim.ts case 'passage' ever changes, the filter fails open and the passage text shows twice (pane + chatter). Export the renderer from the engine (or tag passage events) so web and engine share one source of truth. (2) Reading niceties: optional soft page-turn SFX; widow control so a passage's final page doesn't carry a single orphan line; consider dimming the advance marker on the final page of the final passage. (3) Battle-time passages are currently impossible (interactions are overworld-only) — if a future command can emit passages mid-battle, verify pane-over-battle layering and the exit-battle gating in main.ts loop.

title: Decide: empty-valid catalog (loosen typeChart.types/moves/species min(1))
description: djt.6 mentioned 'catalog optional or empty-valid (typeChart currently requires >=1 type — loosen)'. The engine half shipped catalog-as-optional instead; an empty catalog object still fails CatalogSchema (types/moves/species each min(1)). Decide whether {typeChart:{types:[],effectiveness:{}},moves:[],species:[],items:[]} should ALSO validate as a narrative game (forge blank drafts would then validate earlier). If yes: loosen the min(1)s, treat an empty catalog exactly like an absent one in validateGame/Sim, and keep existing games byte-identical.

title: forge_map: overlay trainer line-of-sight coverage
description: forge_map renders tiles, entities, portals and the encounter table, but a trainer's lineOfSight {dir, range} — the thing that decides whether a route trainer is avoidable — is invisible; in the 85g.6 run the LOS column had to be computed by hand to guarantee the road crossing engages. Suggest marking covered tiles (e.g. '!' or a listed tile range per trainer in the key) so avoidability is visible at a glance.

title: Forge: multi-seed explore sweep for balance tuning (single-level edits perturb the RNG stream)
description: Balance tuning in the 85g.6 run was whack-a-mole: changing one trainer's level reshuffles the deterministic RNG stream, flipping OTHER seeds between win/loss (boss opener 8->7 made seed 1 lose and seed 2 win). Proving robustness meant calling forge_playtest explore 5x with seed 1..5 after every tweak and eyeballing. Wanted: forge_playtest accepting seeds:[...] (or count:N) returning a compact per-seed win/steps/battles table plus aggregate win rate — one call per balance iteration instead of five.

title: Forge: blank template legend lacks ',' road tile named as core vocabulary in the guide
description: forge.md 'Schema conventions' lists the boring shared vocabulary as '# tree/wall, . grass, , road, ~ water, * tall grass' — but the blank template's legend ships only '. # ~ *'. Every blank-start author must addTile ',' themselves before painting the first road (85g.6 run did). Add ',' to the blank template legend (and consider '=' floor / '%' wall too, since the guide recommends them for interiors).

title: Explore report: stopDetail should name the undefeated gate trainer / unmet flag blocking progress
description: When the explorer loses a trainer battle it never re-challenges (see llm-rpg-aiw.18 for the policy fix), and the run ends stopReason=exhausted with stopDetail 'no reachable pending targets left (every reachable entity interacted with in the current flag-state...)'. That wording hides the actual blocker: in the 85g.6 run the real story was 'lost to net-mender-oda; oda_defeated gates knotted-bar which gates the lighthouse'. The static check already knows the flag->gate graph; the explore report should say which lost/unfought trainers set flags that pessimistically gate unreached content.

title: Forge docs: catalog/entity field schemas missing from forge.md; README species example omits required 'types'
description: forge.md's op table names args ('species', 'move', 'item', 'entity', 'tile') without listing their fields, and README's 'Game format in 30 seconds' species example has no types field at all — but addSpecies requires species.types (array). First addSpecies attempt in the 85g.6 run was rejected ('species.types: Required; Unrecognized key type'). Rejection messages do name the fix (good), but the authoring guide should carry a minimal field list per object (species: id, name, types[], glyph, baseStats{hp,atk,def,spd}, learnset, catchRate, xpYield, evolvesTo?; move: id, name, type, power, accuracy, pp, effect?; item: id, name, kind, amount|ballMod; tile: name, glyph, walkable, wild?), and the README example should include types.

title: Forge polish: web hot-reload follow-ups
description:
Follow-ups from llm-rpg-85g.3 (web hot reload + forge overlay), all minor polish:
1. Incompatible-battle path ('reloaded — battle ended, position kept') is implemented (forge.ts battleOk/strip) but was not exercised in the live CDP test — hard to produce a valid game whose catalog breaks only the running battle. Add a targeted test if it matters.
2. Title screen: a forge reload of the current game while the 'Choose Game' chooser is open calls titleScreen.show(), which snaps back to the main menu view.
3. Creating/deleting a whole game dir still triggers a full page reload (Vite glob re-eval) — acceptable for discovery, but could be intercepted too.
4. Forge chip shows validity + time-since-reload only; could also show which file last changed.
5. A stale invalid-game overlay is intentionally NOT cleared by a sprites.json-only save; only the next valid game.json save clears it — document or revisit.

title: Forge: setMeta op (title/goal/version after createGame)
description: Follow-up to llm-rpg-85g.1. No op edits meta after createGame — authors iterating on a goal line or bumping version must hand-edit. Add setMeta(doc, { id?, title?, goal?, version? }) with the usual shallow-merge + schema-order rebuild in forge.ts.

title: Forge: map lifecycle ops (removeMap, renameMap, resizeMap)
description: Follow-up to llm-rpg-85g.1. The edit layer covers createMap + painting but consciously skipped map lifecycle: removeMap (only if unreferenced by portals/player.map/player.respawn, or with a cascade option), renameMap (rewrite portal toMap refs, player.map, respawn.map), and resizeMap (grow/crop rows with a fill char, rejecting crops that would orphan entities/portals). Same ForgeResult contract as forge.ts.

title: Playtest: smarter battler policy for goal mode
description: The explorer's greedy battler (highest-power usable move, no items, no catching, no grinding) loses to tuned trainers (Emberwood explore run: 1 won / 10 lost, stuck at badge_fern). Improvements: type-effectiveness- and accuracy-aware move scoring, heal items in battle, optional catch-to-fill-party, and a grind loop that levels on wild tiles before re-challenging a trainer after a loss. Keep it deterministic (no Math.random).

title: Engine QoL: party reorder action
description: Party order is fixed at catch/gift order, so every fight opens with the original starter and pivots pay a switch-in hit; a reorder action (overworld) would fix it. Overlapping overworld-item-use half of this idea is already tracked by llm-rpg-t9a. Found while playtesting Emberwood (aiw.12).

title: Engine: trainer defeatText prints after rewardCommands (after win text)
description: settleBattle order is defeatFlag -> rewardMoney -> rewardCommands -> defeatText, so a rewardCommands 'win' banner precedes the trainer's defeat line. Emberwood works around it by inlining Vespera's defeat line as the first rewardCommands say and omitting defeatText. Consider emitting defeatText before rewardCommands.

title: Engine: battle can start with a fainted lead active (no forced switch at battle open)
description: If party slot 1 is at 0 HP when a battle begins, it is sent out anyway and the player must burn awkward turns switching; enemy attacks resolve against a fainted combatant. Found while playtesting Emberwood (aiw.12). Suggest: auto-send first healthy member, or set needsSwitch at battle start.

title: Battle screen juice: hit shake, catch-toss animation, blocking dialogue
description: apps/web battle view: add attacker lunge / defender shake on damage, a snare-toss beat for Catch, and optional keypress-to-advance blocking dialogue on the overworld (messages currently auto-advance and never block movement). Also consider trainer name on the enemy panel and party pips for multi-kindred enemy parties.

title: Web UI: responsive stage scaling + in-game credits screen
description: Stage is fixed 768x576; add integer downscale for small screens. Add a credits line/screen reproducing the two CC-BY battler attributions from apps/web/public/assets/LICENSES.md (the file ships in dist, but in-game credit is friendlier).

title: Web UI polish: dedicated sprites for dog/hearth/stalls + distinct NPC palettes
description: The emoji-glyph fallback currently renders Biscuit (dog), the village hearth, the snare-stall, and the east-road sign; the peddler and trailhand both use the same npc1 villager sprite. Add small pixel sprites (dog, campfire, stall, sign) to the manifest and map them in games/demo/sprites.json; palette-swap another villager variant so peddler and trailhand differ.

title: Overworld item use + key items (keepers' charm passive catch bonus)
description: Remainder split out of llm-rpg-aiw.8: (1) using heal items OUTSIDE battle (no overworld 'use item' action exists yet); (2) key-item kind in the item schema with passive effects — keepers' charm boosting catch rate per the Emberwood design bible; (3) optional player-sells-to-shop (buyback) if ever wanted — the sell command is shopkeeper->player only. Heal-center convention already exists (heal_party hearth entity pattern, see demo village hearth).

title: Creature box storage (overflow when party of 6 is full)
description: Catching with a full party currently releases the creature gently (event: 'Your party is full — you let the X slip back into the grass'). Add a box/storage system: caught creatures go to a box instead of being released; add deposit/withdraw interactions (heal-hearth PC pattern). Keep SimState serializable and deterministic.

title: Battler idle animation frames: current 34 battlers are single-frame; source or generate 2+ frame idle anims (bob/breathe) or an animated CC0/CC-BY monster pack; manifest/renderer already support multi-frame idles
Typecheck gate: packages/play fails tsc --noEmit (missing @types/node, no typecheck script)
description: Pre-existing: packages/play has no @types/node devDependency and no typecheck script, so 'npx tsc --noEmit' reports Cannot find module node:fs / process errors. tsx runtime works fine. Add @types/node + a repo-wide typecheck script so type regressions are caught.

title: Title screen, menu, and browser save slots
description: Stretch: title screen with game title art, continue/new-game, localStorage save slots in the web app wrapping engine save/load (aiw.9).
close_reason: Title screen (New Game/Continue/Choose Game, keyboard+click, ember-glow styling), localStorage saves keyed by gameId (3 slots + autosave) over engine save.ts codec, pause panel on P/Esc, game switcher via import.meta.glob + ?game= param, friendly invalid-game error screen. CDP walkthrough on games/demo passed: title→new game→battle win→autosave→reload→Continue restores exact position; 0 console errors; sprites.html untouched.

title: Chiptune audio: data-driven music + SFX (WebAudio)
description: Stretch: WebAudio chiptune player where tracks are data (note event lists in JSON) — town theme, route theme, battle theme, victory sting; SFX for hit/faint/catch/heal. No external audio files needed if synthesized.
close_reason: WebAudio chiptune engine, all content in apps/web/src/audio/tracks.json: town/route/battle loops + victory sting (two voices each, midi note events), 7 SFX one-shots, map-substring→track mapping with default. Autoplay-safe lazy AudioContext, crossfade on scene change, victory sting ducks music, M mute toggle persisted. Verified headless: scheduling ran (gated ?audiodebug logs), no exceptions.

title: Autoplay playtest harness
description: Agent-facing harness that plays a game to completion (or reports where it got stuck): scripted goals, step budget, transcript output. The build-side QA loop.
close_reason: Playtest harness shipped: packages/play/src/playtest.ts (script + goal=explore modes, JSONL transcripts, exit 0 only on win) and autoplay.ts (deterministic BFS explorer + greedy battler). Regression tests in packages/engine/test/emberwood.test.ts pin Emberwood README script win at turn 1242 and demo explorability. 110 tests green, tsc clean. Verified: emberwood script WIN (1250/1251 steps), emberwood explore covers 5/7 maps and diagnoses the badge_fern battle wall, demo explore WINs in 41 steps.

title: Playtest: script-mode divergence diagnostics
description: When a previously-winning script stops winning after a content edit, the report shows where it ended but not where it first diverged. Add an optional --expect <transcript.jsonl> that replays against a recorded transcript and reports the first step whose events differ.

title: Emberwood content polish (v0.2 ideas)
description: Skipped polish from aiw.12: more badge-reactive dialogue beyond Petra/Wick; names for Vespera's kindred (the 'V & T' brazier hints a story); a second Mistmarsh gift/loop so the wet route feels less linear; re-aim Juna/Rooke lineOfSight to cross the main walking line; possible 'revive ember' item kind if the engine grows one; kiln-interior decor tiles.

title: Audio polish: title ambience, catch-fail/run SFX, per-game track overrides in games/<id>
description: Follow-up from aiw.15: title screen is silent by design; add a soft hearth ambience. SFX exist for hit/faint/catch/heal/level-up but not catch-broke-free or escape. Consider letting a game ship its own tracks.json overrides.

title: Web polish: replace native confirm()/R dialog with in-UI prompt; allow pause+save during battle
description: Follow-up from aiw.16: R-to-title currently uses window.confirm (blocks headless testing, breaks tone); pause panel is overworld-only even though engine snapshots support mid-battle saves (mid-battle restore already works via beginPlay).
